equities.name: TSX Composite
equities.context: The TSX Composite closed at 34,937.90 on June 12, advancing 1.52% on the week and 31.27% year-over-year — the index extended a multi-quarter climb as gold settled at US$4,353.30/oz (+26.87% year-over-year) and copper at US$6.5085/lb (+35.59% year-over-year), supplying the materials sub-index its largest annual gain since the 2020-21 commodity cycle.37 Energy sub-index components faced an offset as WTI fell 11.74% on the week to US$80.58/bbl, reflecting a partial reversal of the recent supply-shock premium that had carried crude above US$100/bbl a month earlier.37 Financials drew support from the Bank of Canada holding the overnight rate at 2.25% on June 10 for the second consecutive decision, anchoring the front of the Government of Canada curve while the 5Y benchmark held at 3.04%.1 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the index move to 635 active Canadian mining projects ($184.5B aggregate) and 936 power and energy projects ($614.3B), alongside 89 oil and gas projects ($63.5B) whose netbacks track the WTI decline.37 If gold holds above US$4,200/oz through the third quarter, the 635 mining projects would maintain the all-in sustaining cost coverage cited in 2025 securities filings for Canadian gold producers.37

equities.name: S&P 500
equities.context: The S&P 500 closed at 7,431.46 on June 12, up 0.65% on the week and 22.93% year-over-year — the advance came as positioning firmed ahead of the June 16-17 FOMC meeting and Summary of Economic Projections, the first decision under new Chair Kevin Warsh, with market pricing reflecting a hold at the 3.50-3.75% target range.21 The annual gain marks the index's largest 52-week percentage advance since the post-pandemic recovery window of 2020-21, driven by Q1 GDP at +2.6% per the Philadelphia Fed Survey of Professional Forecasters and core CPI at +2.6% year-over-year in the March reference.2223

equities.name: Dow Jones
equities.context: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 51,202.26 on June 12, up 0.66% on the week and 19.16% year-over-year — industrial and healthcare components carried the weekly move as US unemployment held at 4.4% in the May Bureau of Labor Statistics print, following first-quarter private payroll growth running more than 2.5 times the 2025 monthly average.24 The 19.16% year-over-year advance trails the broader S&P 500 by roughly four percentage points but stands as the index's largest annual gain since the post-pandemic recovery, with positioning measured ahead of the FOMC SEP release scheduled for June 17.21

equities.name: NASDAQ
equities.context: The NASDAQ Composite closed at 25,888.84 on June 12, up 0.70% on the week and 31.67% year-over-year — the technology-heavy index posted the steepest 52-week percentage gain of the four North American benchmarks tracked here, as positioning held ahead of the June 16-17 FOMC decision and amid sustained earnings momentum across mega-cap technology constituents.21 The annual advance matches the TSX Composite's 31.27% gain almost basis-point for basis-point, the closest cross-border parity recorded since early 2021.37
